statement: Let L be the least positive integer divisible by both divisor1 and divisor2. For every positive integer M, there exist finite sets A and B of positive integers with |A| = unique_cnt1, |B| = unique_cnt2, every a in A not divisible by divisor1, every b in B not divisible by divisor2, A and B disjoint, and every x in A union B satisfying x <= M if and only if M - floor(M / divisor1) >= unique_cnt1, M - floor(M / divisor2) >= unique_cnt2, and M - floor(M / L) >= unique_cnt1 + unique_cnt2. Consequently, whenever minimize_set divisor1 divisor2 unique_cnt1 unique_cnt2 returns r, r is the least positive integer satisfying these three counting inequalities.
